page: Amazon Web Services i3en.24xlarge is a high-density, storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features dual-socket Intel Xeon 8259CL processors delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8.0 GB per physical core allocation ratio. The instance does not incorporate discrete GPU accelerators, focusing entirely on high-capacity storage and multi-threaded computation.

Storage and networking are the defining architectural pillars of this instance. It includes 60,000 GB (60 TB) of local NVMe SSD storage bundled directly into the hardware configuration, alongside 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI, though modern acceleration sets like AMX, AVX-VNNI, and AVX-512 VNNI are absent. Single-threaded performance lands in the lower tiers, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core (1387.4) and gzip compression (23.57 GB/sec). However, multi-threaded CPU and memory metrics show exceptional scale, with stress-ng multi-core achieving 81,307.29 and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 219.74 GB/sec.

Given its immense 60 TB NVMe storage footprint, 100 Gbps network capacity, and 768 GB memory footprint, the i3en.24xlarge delivers strong cost efficiency for high-density transactional systems that would otherwise require multiple smaller instances or expensive external block storage arrays. It is poorly matched for single-threaded processing or low-latency generative LLM inference, as shown by token generation rates (5.49 tokens/sec on 7B models). The instance is best suited for distributed file systems, high-throughput NoSQL databases like Cassandra and MongoDB, data warehousing, search indexing clusters such as Elasticsearch, and large-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered for I/O-intensive workloads requiring vast local storage and high network throughput. Driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processors, 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and no GPUs. Its hardware profile is anchored by 60,000 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline networking. While single-threaded benchmarks reflect moderate core speeds, multi-threaded tests, memory bandwidth (219.74 GB/sec uncached reads), and Redis throughput (75.3 million ops/sec) sit in the top performance tiers. The instance provides strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for massive datasets, making it an appropriate platform for distributed NoSQL databases, search engines, analytics clusters, and large-scale data processing.
